title: The whisper
hook: Shaytan whispers to them both and they eat, and their shame appears (7:20–22)

segments.voice: Yesterday: khalifah, and the garden's one tree. Everything given freely, and a single limit. Your line was everything, minus one. Did you count what you have? Day twenty-six.

It's two in the morning and you can't sleep. A voice in your head starts up. Not loud. It never shouts. Just reasonable. You know, one more episode won't hurt. Actually, you deserve that. Or the other kind: they were laughing at you, weren't they. You'll never be good enough. It sounds exactly like your own voice. That's what makes it work. Today, the garden has everything, and one tree, and then someone starts to talk. Not with a shout, or a threat. With a whisper.
screen: `TWO IN THE MORNING.` → `A REASONABLE LITTLE VOICE.` → `IT SOUNDS LIKE YOU.`

segments.voice: Surah seven, verse twenty: “Then Satan whispered to them.” The Arabic verb is waswasa, and listen to it: was-was. The word itself whispers. It's the sound of lips close to an ear. What did he say? Notice the method. He didn't say, disobey God. He renamed the tree. In another surah, he calls it the tree of immortality, and a kingdom that never wears out. Your Lord only forbade it, he says, so you wouldn't become angels, or live forever. Then he swore to them that he was a sincere adviser. The forbidden thing, dressed up as a gift. A limit, dressed up as God holding out on you. And they ate, and at once their shame appeared to them, and they began covering themselves with leaves of the garden. Here's a detail readers often miss. In surah seven, the whisper, the eating and the shame are all told in the Arabic dual: the two of them. The Qur'an doesn't pin it on the woman. The whisper came to both, and both ate. The Qur'an's last surah names this voice: in Pickthall's words, “the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind.” In Arabic, al-waswas al-khannas, the whisperer who slinks back. Many commentators explain: it retreats when God is remembered, and comes back when you forget. And a hadith in Bukhari brings real relief: God has forgiven people what their own souls whisper to them, as long as they don't act on it or say it. The whisper isn't the wrong. Following it is. So the thought at two in the morning isn't a verdict on you. It's just a voice. And not every voice is yours.
screen: `WASWAS — THE WORD WHISPERS.` · `HE RENAMED THE TREE.` · `THE WHISPER CAME TO BOTH.` · `THE WHISPERER WHO SLINKS BACK.` · then, large: `THEN SATAN WHISPERED TO THEM.`

segments.voice: The bell will give you two minutes. Sit quietly, and just listen to your own mind. Thoughts will come. Some will be kind, some will be sharp, some will be selling you something. Don't argue with any of them. When one comes that pulls at you, a craving, a cruel line about yourself, a grudge, just label it softly: whisper. And let it pass, like a car going by outside. If you pray, you can say a'udhu billah, I seek refuge in God, the words Muslims use when a whisper comes. The bell holds the time.
Waswas. The whisper: a quiet voice that renames the tree and sounds like your own. The whisperer slinks back when God is remembered.
Your line: not every voice is yours. Today, catch one whisper, the craving, the cruel line, the grudge, and let it pass without doing what it says. Day twenty-six.

howItsDone: When Muslims feel an evil or anxious whisper, many say a'udhu billahi mina sh-shaytani r-rajim, I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, and recite the last two surahs, al-Falaq and an-Nas.

original.note: Arabic: the whisperer, the whispering; the sound of the word imitates a whisper.

trapdoor: what you thought: the devil tempted Eve, and Eve tempted Adam.
what it means: waswas — the whisper came to both, renaming the forbidden as a gift, and both ate.

what a scholar hears: surah seven tells it in the Arabic dual, the two of them; the word waswas imitates its own sound; and 114:4 calls it al-waswas al-khannas, the whisperer who slinks back at the remembrance of God.

sources.quoted: the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind

sources.ref: Qur'an 7:20–22; 20:120–121 (the tree renamed; the oath; the eating and the leaves)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2528 (what the soul whispers is forgiven unless acted on or spoken)

notes: Pickthall 7:20 and 114:4–5 quoted from memory ('From the evil of the sneaking whisperer, Who whispereth in the hearts of mankind,'). Confirm.
The dual: in 7:20–22 the whisper, the eating and the shame are in the dual; 20:120–121 addresses the whisper to Adam and says Adam disobeyed. The script says 'in surah seven'. Confirm.
Al-khannas: retreating when God is remembered is the common explanation (Ibn 'Abbas via al-Tabari). Confirm.
Waswas is onomatopoeic according to Arabic philologists; confirm the claim.
The practice mentions a'udhu billah as what Muslims say, offered as an invitation; it's the standard formula (16:98), not a new prayer.
